MUPPET Model Checking

MUPPET.model.checking.Rd

Conduct posterior predictive model checking. This is an internal function called by MUPPET.modular, and is not intended to be called directly by users.

Usage

MUPPET.model.checking(
  fragments,
  which.fragment,
  n.estimation.batches,
  iters.per.batch,
  home.folder,
  n.model.check.iterations,
  save.post.pred.data,
  save.summary.stats.from.model.check,
  save.summary.plots.from.model.check,
  retain.model.check.iteration.files
)

Arguments

fragments

A list with elements defining the model fragments. Each element in this list contains a set of specifications for the corresponding fragment. The 1st element in this list pertains to the 1st fragment, the 2nd element in this list pertains to the 2nd fragment, and so on. The order of the list also communicates the order each model fragment will be fit. Each element of this list is itself a list with specifications for the fragment. Each set of specifications can include:

  • name: Character, giving a name to the fragment. No default. If nothing is supplied, the fragment name will be the fragment number.

  • fragment.folder: Character, giving the name of the folder to be created storing the results for the fragment. If no value is supplied, will default to a name made up of the fragment number and fragment name.

  • model.syntax: Character, containing syntax for the Mplus MODEL statement.

  • variable.syntax: Character, containing syntax for the Mplus VARIABLE statement.

  • priors.syntax: Character, expression containing Mplus syntax for the prior specifications for the model in this fragment, corresponding to the Mplus MODELPRIORS statement. If nothing is specified, defaults to using Mplus's default priors.

  • conditioning: Number, or vector of numbers, indicating which fragments to condition on when fitting this fragment. Examples: a value of 0 indicates the fragment is unconditional; a value of 1 indicates the fragment is conditional on the first fragment in the fragments list; a value of c(1, 2) indicates the fragment is conditional on fragment 1 and fragment 2 in the fragments list.

  • parameters.to.exclude.in.conditioning: A list, of length equal to the number of fragments that are conditioned on (i.e., the length of the collection supplied as the argument for conditioning). Each element of the list is a character, or character vector, naming the kinds of parameters from the associated antecedent fragment that should be ignored in fitting this fragment. Possible values are:

    • "none"

    • "loadings"

    • "(co)variances of observables"

    • "means and intercepts of observables"

    • "thresholds"

    • "structural coefficients"

    • "(co)variances of latent variables"

    • "means and intercepts of latent variables"

    A value of "none" indicates that all fitted parameters from the antecedent fragment should be conditioned on. For example, if conditioning = c(1,2), and parameters.to.exclude.in.conditioning = list("none", c("(co)variances of latent variables", "means and intercepts of latent variables")), then none of the parameters from fragment 1 will be ignored, while there will be parameters from fragment 2 that are ignored. These parameters include the (co)variances of latent variables and the means and intercepts of latent variables. If no value for parameters.to.exclude.in.conditioning is supplied, the default is "none" for all antecedent fragments.

  • to.fit: Logical, indicating if this fragment should be fit. If no value is supplied, defaults to TRUE. If value is FALSE, the fragment will not be fit. This can be useful when a fragment has previously been fit, and is now being used as an antecdent to another fragment.

  • estimating.lvs: Logical, indicating if this fragment pertains to estimating latent variable values. Default is FALSE. But using default may be finicky, so recommend specifying explicitly. estimating.lvs = TRUE should not be specified for unconditional fragment.

  • data: The dataset to use in fitting this fragment.

  • model.check.this.fragment: Logical, indicating if model checking should be conducted for this fragment. If no value is supplied, defaults to the value of model.check. Model checking is only available when estimating.lvs = FALSE.

which.fragment

The fragment number for which model checking is conducted.

n.estimation.batches

The number of estimation batches when fitting fragments that are conditional on antecedent fragments. Default is NULL, in which case the function will divide the total number of post burn-in iterations by 1000, effectively doing batches of 1000 iterations at a time. Using more estimation batches leads to fewer iterations per estimation batch. This can be helpful for reducing computational burden and run time, and also offers future possibilities for checkpointing.

If n.estimation.batches is specified, the total number of post burn-in iterations must be a multiple of n.estimation.batches. If left as NULL, the total number of post burn-in iterations must be a multiple of 1000 when exceeding 1000 iterations, otherwise, a single batch is used.

iters.per.batch

Number of iterations per batch, calculated in MUPPET.modular.

home.folder

Working directory obtained from getwd() in MUPPET.modular.

n.model.check.iterations

Number of iterations (number of posterior predicted datasets) used in model checking. Default to use all iterations.

save.post.pred.data

Logical, indicating if posterior predicted datasets from the model checking procedure should be saved. Default is FALSE.

save.summary.stats.from.model.check

Logical, indicating if numerical summaries of model checking should be saved. Default is TRUE.

save.summary.plots.from.model.check

Logical, indicating if plots of model checking should be saved. Default is TRUE.

retain.model.check.iteration.files

Logical. Should the iteration-specific files be saved when conducting model checking? If set to FALSE, will still save the simulation-related files for iteration 1, which may be useful for troubleshooting if needed. Default is FALSE.

Value

Model checking progress and completion messages. Model checking output files will be written out to the hard drive.
